## System Architecture {#system-architecture}

The MediaWiki instance follows a containerized microservices architecture with clear separation between development, staging, and production environments.

```{mermaid}
graph TB
    subgraph "External Access"
        User[👤 End Users]
        Admin[👨‍💻 Administrators]
        Researcher[👨‍🔬 Researchers]
    end

    subgraph "Load Balancer / Reverse Proxy"
        Caddy[🔄 Caddy Proxy<br/>SSL Termination]
    end

    subgraph "Application Layer"
        MW_Prod[📖 MediaWiki Production<br/>Port 8080]
        MW_Staging[📖 MediaWiki Staging<br/>Port 8081]
        PhpMyAdmin[🗄️ phpMyAdmin<br/>Port 8082]
        FileServer[📁 Caddy File Server<br/>Port 8090]
    end

    subgraph "Database Layer"
        DB_Prod[(🗄️ MariaDB Production<br/>my_wiki)]
        DB_Staging[(🗄️ MariaDB Staging<br/>my_wiki)]
    end

    subgraph "Storage Layer"
        Images_Prod[📁 Production Images<br/>./mediawiki_images]
        Images_Staging[📁 Staging Images<br/>./staging_mediawiki_images]
        DB_Data_Prod[💾 Production DB Data<br/>./db_data]
        DB_Data_Staging[💾 Staging DB Data<br/>./staging_db_data]
        Backups[💾 Backup Storage<br/>./backups]
        ClusterWork[📁 Cluster Work Files<br/>/cluster/work/histuzh]
    end

    User --> Caddy
    Admin --> Caddy
    Researcher --> Caddy

    Caddy --> MW_Prod
    Caddy --> MW_Staging
    Admin --> PhpMyAdmin
    Admin --> FileServer

    MW_Prod --> DB_Prod
    MW_Staging --> DB_Staging

    MW_Prod --> Images_Prod
    MW_Staging --> Images_Staging

    DB_Prod --> DB_Data_Prod
    DB_Staging --> DB_Data_Staging

    PhpMyAdmin --> DB_Staging
    FileServer --> ClusterWork

    style MW_Prod fill:#e1f5fe
    style MW_Staging fill:#fff3e0
    style DB_Prod fill:#e8f5e8
    style DB_Staging fill:#fff8e1
    style Caddy fill:#f3e5f5
```

## Deployment Environments {#deployment-environments}

The system supports three main environments with different purposes and configurations:

```{mermaid}
graph LR
    subgraph "Development Environment"
        Dev[🛠️ Development<br/>Local Docker Build<br/>Live Reload<br/>Debug Mode]
    end

    subgraph "Staging Environment"
        Staging[🧪 Staging<br/>Production Mirror<br/>Testing & QA<br/>Data Sync from Prod]
    end

    subgraph "Production Environment"
        Prod[🚀 Production<br/>Live System<br/>User Access<br/>Research Data]
    end

    Dev -->|Deploy & Test| Staging
    Staging -->|Validate & Promote| Prod
    Prod -->|Data Sync| Staging

    style Dev fill:#e3f2fd
    style Staging fill:#fff3e0
    style Prod fill:#e8f5e8
```

### Environment Details

| Environment | Port | Purpose | Docker Compose File | Database |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| Development | 8080 | Local development and testing | `docker-compose.dev.yml` | `db_data` (volume) |
| Staging | 8081 | Pre-production testing | `docker-compose.prod.yml` | `staging_db_data` |
| Production | 8080 | Live research environment | `docker-compose.prod.yml` | `db_data` |

## Development Workflow {#development-workflow}

The development workflow follows containerized development practices with live reload capabilities:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    Start([👨‍💻 Developer Starts Work]) --> Clone[📥 Clone Repository]
    Clone --> EnvSetup[⚙️ Setup .env File]
    EnvSetup --> DevBuild[🔨 docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml up --build]

    DevBuild --> DevRunning{🏃 Development Environment Running}
    DevRunning --> |Yes| DevWork[💻 Development Work]
    DevRunning --> |No| Troubleshoot[🔧 Troubleshoot Issues]

    DevWork --> CodeChange[📝 Make Code Changes]
    CodeChange --> Test[🧪 Test Changes]
    Test --> Validate{✅ Changes Valid?}

    Validate --> |No| CodeChange
    Validate --> |Yes| Commit[💾 Commit Changes]

    Commit --> Push[📤 Push to GitHub]
    Push --> PR[🔄 Create Pull Request]

    PR --> Review[👀 Code Review]
    Review --> Approved{✅ Approved?}

    Approved --> |No| CodeChange
    Approved --> |Yes| Merge[🔀 Merge to Main]

    Merge --> StagingDeploy[🚀 Deploy to Staging]
    StagingDeploy --> StagingTest[🧪 Staging Testing]
    StagingTest --> ProdDeploy[🏭 Production Deployment]

    Troubleshoot --> DevBuild

    style Start fill:#e3f2fd
    style DevRunning fill:#fff3e0
    style Validate fill:#e8f5e8
    style Approved fill:#e8f5e8
```

### Development Commands

``` bash
# Start development environment
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build

# View logs
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml logs -f

# Update database schema
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml exec mediawiki php maintenance/update.php --quick

# Run queue jobs
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.dev.yml exec mediawiki php maintenance/runJobs.php --maxjobs=1000
```

## Production Deployment {#production-deployment}

Production deployment follows a systematic approach ensuring high availability and data integrity:

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
    PrepImage[🔨 Build Docker Image<br/>docker build -f deployment/Dockerfile -t mediawiki:latest .]
    SaveImage[💾 Save Image<br/>docker image save mediawiki -o mediawiki_image.tar]

    subgraph "Target Server Preparation"
        TransferImage[📤 Transfer Image to Server<br/>scp/rsync]
        LoadImage[📥 Load Image<br/>docker load < mediawiki_image.tar]
        EnvConfig[⚙️ Configure Environment<br/>.env file setup]
    end

    subgraph "Pre-Deployment Checks"
        BackupCheck[💾 Verify Backup System]
        ResourceCheck[🔍 Check Server Resources]
        AccessCheck[🔐 Verify Access Permissions]
    end

    subgraph "Deployment Execution"
        StopServices[⏹️ Stop Existing Services<br/>docker-compose down]
        StartServices[▶️ Start New Services<br/>docker-compose up -d]
        HealthCheck[🏥 Health Check Services]
    end

    subgraph "Post-Deployment"
        SchemaUpdate[🔄 Update Database Schema<br/>maintenance/update.php]
        QueueJobs[⚡ Process Queue Jobs<br/>maintenance/runJobs.php]
        FinalTest[✅ Final Validation Tests]
    end

    PrepImage --> SaveImage
    SaveImage --> TransferImage
    TransferImage --> LoadImage
    LoadImage --> EnvConfig

    EnvConfig --> BackupCheck
    BackupCheck --> ResourceCheck
    ResourceCheck --> AccessCheck

    AccessCheck --> StopServices
    StopServices --> StartServices
    StartServices --> HealthCheck

    HealthCheck --> SchemaUpdate
    SchemaUpdate --> QueueJobs
    QueueJobs --> FinalTest

    HealthCheck --> |Failed| StopServices
    FinalTest --> |Failed| StopServices

    style PrepImage fill:#e3f2fd
    style HealthCheck fill:#fff3e0
    style FinalTest fill:#e8f5e8
```

### Production Deployment Commands

``` bash
# 1. Build and save image (local) - Dockerfile is in deployment directory
docker build -f deployment/Dockerfile -t mediawiki:latest .
docker image save mediawiki -o mediawiki_image.tar

# 2. Transfer to production server
rsync -av -e "ssh -J user@jump-server" ./mediawiki_image.tar server-user@prod-server:/path/

# 3. Deploy on production server
docker load < mediawiki_image.tar
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.prod.yml up -d

# 4. Post-deployment tasks
docker exec mediawiki php maintenance/update.php --quick
docker exec mediawiki php maintenance/runJobs.php --maxjobs=1000
```

## Infrastructure Components {#infrastructure-components}

The system consists of several containerized components working together, built from a custom Dockerfile that includes all necessary MediaWiki extensions and configurations.

### Dockerfile Configuration

The deployment includes a custom Dockerfile (`deployment/Dockerfile`) that extends the official MediaWiki 1.43.1 image with:

-   **MediaWiki Extensions**: Cargo, DataTransfer, PageForms, PageSchemas, and PdfBook extensions
-   **System Packages**: Git, OpenSSL, and htmldoc for enhanced functionality
-   **Custom Assets**: UZH logo integration
-   **Proper Permissions**: Configured file permissions for web server access

``` dockerfile
FROM mediawiki:1.43.1

# Install necessary packages for MediaWiki extensions
RUN echo "deb https://deb.debian.org/debian/ bookworm main contrib non-free" >> /etc/apt/sources.list && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git openssl htmldoc && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install MediaWiki extensions from official repositories
RUN git clone -b REL1_43 https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/mediawiki/extensions/Cargo /var/www/html/extensions/Cargo
RUN git clone -b REL1_43 https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/mediawiki/extensions/DataTransfer /var/www/html/extensions/DataTransfer
RUN git clone -b REL1_43 https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/mediawiki/extensions/PageForms /var/www/html/extensions/PageForms
RUN git clone -b REL1_43 https://gerrit.wikimedia.org/r/mediawiki/extensions/PageSchemas /var/www/html/extensions/PageSchemas
RUN git clone https://github.com/debtcompliance/PdfBook/ /var/www/html/extensions/PdfBook

# Integrate custom branding assets
COPY assets/uzh-logo.svg /var/www/html/resources/assets/uzh-logo.svg
RUN chown www-data:www-data /var/www/html/resources/assets/uzh-logo.svg

# Set proper permissions for MediaWiki
RUN chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/html/extensions
```

### Troubleshooting Commands

``` bash
# Check service status
docker ps -a
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.prod.yml ps

# View detailed logs
docker logs mediawiki --tail 100
docker logs db --tail 100

# Restart services
docker-compose -f deployment/docker-compose.prod.yml restart

# Clean up resources
docker system prune -f
docker volume prune -f

# Check database connectivity
docker exec -it db mariadb -u wikiuser -p -e "SHOW DATABASES;"

# Reset permissions
docker exec -it mediawiki chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/html/images
```
